text:
devops_jess: Heads-up — noticed repeated scale-ups in ap-southeast-1 last night where CA kept spinning up small GPU nodes and then tearing them down a few minutes later. Adds ~30% cost spike for the window. Anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

k8s_tim: Seen similar in metrics. Looks like binpack/least-waste expander choice + low scale-down-unneeded-time causing oscillation. Logs show a lot of short-lived pods (preprocessing jobs) and a couple of PDB-blocked pods preventing clean drains.

enginfra_rolf: Any chance these are from our spot/preemptible mix? Preempts + quick resched -> CA thinks capacity needed and triggers new nodes.

devops_jess: Yes, most of the nodes were spot. Node events show termination notices followed by CA replacements. Example from autoscaler: 
```
I0615 03:12:10 scale_up.go:xxx] Upcoming nodes: 2 (gpu-pool-apac: 2)
I0615 03:14:20 scale_down.go:yyy] Node gpu-spot-abc terminated, delay before delete 2m
```

sre_maya: Quick thoughts: increase --scale-down-unneeded-time to 10m or 15m, bump --scale-down-utilization-threshold to 0.6, and set --max-empty-bulk-delete to 5. Also consider --max-node-provision-time=20m so CA waits longer for nodes to come healthy before triggering new launches.

k8s_tim: Also try switching expander to "most-pods" or "price" for the GPU pools so it prefers nodes that consolidate pods more vs spreading small pods across many nodes. Our current expander is "least-waste" which is susceptible when pods are bursty.

enginfra_rolf: For GPU-specific pools we should probably disable scale-to-zero entirely for critical worker pools (label: workload=gpu-batch-critical) — scale-to-zero + sporadic batch jobs = churn. Marking those nodegroups as min=1 helped on staging.

devops_jess: Good call. What about PDBs? We're seeing blocked drains because a couple of long-lived infra pods are on those nodes.

sre_maya: Two options: kube-pdb relax (lower minAvailable) or add drain-ignore annotation for non-critical pods. But safer: mark those infra pods with nodeAffinity to non-gpu nodes so CA can safely remove GPU nodes. Short-term, increase --scale-down-delay-after-add to 12m so newly added nodes aren't considered for scale-down immediately.

k8s_tim: Config snippet I'm leaning to (we can tweak):
```yaml
clusterAutoscaler:
  expander: "most-pods"
  extraArgs:
    scale-down-unneeded-time: "10m"
    scale-down-unready-time: "20m"
    scale-down-delay-after-add: "12m"
    scale-down-utilization-threshold: "0.6"
    max-node-provision-time: "20m"
    max-empty-bulk-delete: "5"
    balance-similar-node-groups: "true"
```

devops_jess: I like that. Let's test on canary (ap-southeast-1a) GPU nodegroup first. Also, can we add a CA metric alert when >3 scale-up events in 15m? capacity_bot: will emit. :robot_face:

capacity_bot: Alert created: CA-high-churn-apac — triggers when autoscaler scale_up_count > 3 in 15m for ap-southeast-1. Escalation: #eng-infra on-call.

enginfra_rolf: One more nuance: balance-similar-node-groups helps cross-AZ packing, but if AZ capacities are skewed it can oscillate. If canary shows improvement, we'll keep it; if not, we might force weighted expander priority with cost weight favoring non-spot for critical pools.

sre_maya: Agreed. After deploy, watch these signals: scale_up_count, scale_down_count, node_lifecycle_time, and per-node GPU utilization (avg over 10m). Also check PDB evictions prevented metric.

devops_jess: Plan: roll CA flags to canary tonight (22:00 UTC), monitor for 2h, rollback if scale_up_count > 5 or cost delta > 15% vs baseline. I'll post results here. Thanks all :raised_hands:
